title: Book II, Aphorisms XI–XX
author: Francis Bacon
source: *Novum Organum*, Book II, Aphorisms XI–XX, in the English translation edited by Joseph Devey (New York: P. F. Collier & Son, 1902), 121–159. Bacon published the *Novum Organum* in Latin in 1620.
summary: The method at work on the nature of heat: tables of presence, of absence in proximate instances, and of degrees, then the exclusion of natures that are not its form, ending in a first vintage, or provisional interpretation, that heat is an expansive and restrained motion striving through the smaller parts of bodies.
